reverse.target: Derivation mechanism chosen at [Q2]: kind comes from the top content directory. It implements no requirement of its own; it is how BR1.1's boundary yields two typed streams.

NFR8 — the published slug rule. NFR8 is site-wide rather than assigned to U1 in the story map, so it is not in this unit's upstream set, but U1 is where the rule is enforced because U1 owns content discovery.
NFR8 — slug uniqueness is the precondition for slug stability. Same reason as BR1.4: enforced here, owned site-wide.

FR2.2 — post ordering is assigned to U2 in the story map. U1 establishes the rule because PostCatalog's ordering must exist for Home (BR5.3) to take the three most recent; U2 completes the Writing list that consumes it.
FR3.4 — the live-URL omit behaviour is assigned to U3. U1 states it because the skeleton serves one project page with its rail, and a rail rendered without the rule would ship an empty row.
ADR-004 — validation runs inside the build. A sequencing constraint on how the build is structured rather than a requirement it satisfies; it exists so no invocation path can skip validation.

NFR1 — WCAG 2.1 AA keyboard operation, assigned to U5 in the story map. U1 emits the skip link and its document position because U5 cannot add a link the templates never render; U5 supplies the visible-on-focus treatment.

NFR3 and NFR4 — the no-third-party rule and its content-security-policy tag, assigned to U5 in the story map. U1 emits the tag because it is condition 6 of the walking skeleton's definition of done; U5 must keep the policy holding once a stylesheet and font are added.
